epic.title: Epic #418 redux — engine projection and completeness defects
epic.intent_and_why: Close the class of Task fields the engine carries but never projects, so a gate's standing instruction actually reaches the agent it binds.

definition_of_done: The completeness property that guards the field class is capable of failing, and has been observed failing.
The schema record describes shipped behaviour.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: No check that cannot fail; every red-proof reproduced in the Commander's own hands and the tree restored byte-identical.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Broad-suite green with the real exit code, plus a deliberate break that turns the property red by name.

hard_constraints: Own scripts/checklist_engine.py only; do not edit scripts/collect_feedback.py, episodes/, or scripts/verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py.
Do not rebase or merge main; the Admiral replants the branch.
The doc describes shipped behaviour; it never becomes the enforcement mechanism.
fixed_decisions: Inventory verdict is RENDER, not delete: 8 populated corpus blocks, three of them in shipped spine templates.
The completeness property's extractor stays INDEPENDENT of the renderer, so one bug cannot render nothing and assert nothing in agreement.

current_wave.objective: Render `directives` and close the unrendered-field class.
exit_criteria: g1 renders both live shapes with a golden captured RED first.
g2 ships a completeness property with a total extractor, a per-field ledger, a builder-superset assertion and an in-suite negative self-test.
g3 corrects the drifted schema row and the false Rendering claim.
Broad suite green at or above the recorded baseline with the real exit code.

issues.title: Render `directives` in the engine's `current` projection
issues.desired_outcome: A populated `directives` block reaches the agent the gate binds, and the field class is guarded by a property that can actually go red.
issues.useful_now: Three shipped spine templates carry the field, so every run instantiated from them silently loses its standing contract.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: Before/after `current` on a populated block; the property observed failing by field name when a populated field is deliberately unrendered.
issues.implementation_latitude: Renderer internals free; the projection's existing omit-when-empty contract is preserved.
hard_constraints_no_gos: No shared helper between the property's leaf extractor and the renderer.
No check that reports green without asserting anything.

wave_forecast.outcome: Wire the gauge writer hook so a fresh dispatch does not inherit its predecessor's context reading
wave_forecast.why_likely: Observed to cost real time on this run; #180's settings.json wiring is already a known open item
entry_conditions: A human decides the wiring, since it touches settings.json

uncertainty_register.unknown: Whether template-only Task fields need their own guard
uncertainty_register.affects: How completely the unrendered-field class is actually closed
uncertainty_register.settle_by: A survey of fields that appear in shipped checklist JSON but in neither the amend-task builder nor `append()`
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: The property's superset assertion covers engine-introduced fields only; the limit is stated in the docstring and in the schema doc
uncertainty_register.next_probe: Diff the union of template gate keys against the builder's key set

parked_possibilities: Rendering satisfied conditions (the satisfied-hiding behaviour is pre-existing and out of this issue's scope)

completed_outcomes.outcome: g1 -- `state()` passes `directives` through and `render_human()` emits the block between `anchors:` and `next:`; both live shapes served (key-to-nested-contract-dict, which all 8 populated corpus gates carry, and the flat `[string]` the schema declares and the add/rescope amend ops build); absent, empty and unrecognized shapes add zero output. g2 -- the field class is closed by a property that can actually fail: `directives` un-excluded from TaskFieldCompleteness, `_flatten` replaced by a total recursive leaf extractor, the single `checked_any` flag replaced by a per-field ledger that names the offending field, the fixture's key set asserted a superset of the engine's own `_build_amend_task`, and an in-suite negative self-test added. g3 -- docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md corrected in both pinned places: the Task table's `directives` row now declares the dict shape, and the Rendering section states positively that a populated `directives` block renders, replacing a false 'Known gap, not yet closed' claim.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Broad suite 1731 passed / 4 skipped / 647 subtests, REAL_EXIT=0 (baseline 1721/4/643). evidence/g1-before-after-current.txt (corpus-wide: 370 files, 2981 gates, exactly 8 gates change output, 0 first lines change); evidence/g1-RED-capture.txt and evidence/g1-integrate-commander-red-reproduction.txt (golden captured RED before the renderer existed); evidence/g2-r2-extractor-blind-to-dicts.txt, evidence/g2-r4-populated-field-flattens-to-nothing.txt, evidence/g2-r5-engine-field-forgotten-in-fixture.txt, evidence/g2-integrate-commander-red-reproduction.txt and evidence/g2-integrate-successor-commander-verification.txt (the property observed FAILING by field name, tree restored byte-identical ef979b43); evidence/g3-schema-doc-correction.txt (pinned c1/c2 greps exit 0).

wave_evidence.claim: A populated `directives` block now reaches the agent the gate binds.
wave_evidence.expected: The block appears in `current` for populated gates and nowhere else.
wave_evidence.observed: Corpus-wide: 370 checklist files, 2981 gates, exactly 8 gates change output — the 8 with a populated block — and 0 first lines change. This run's own spine `execute` gate renders its `replan_input` contract.

wave_evidence.claim: The completeness property is capable of failing, not merely observed passing.
wave_evidence.expected: Deliberately unrendering a populated field turns it red, naming the field.
wave_evidence.observed: Nulling the `directives` passthrough in `state()` fails the property with `populated field 'directives' ... missing from current()'s output`, exit 1, while `constraints:` and `anchors:` still render in the same failure message — so neither field covers for it. Reproduced independently by the implementer, a cold reviewer, and two successive Commanders.

discrepancies.signal: Simply un-excluding `directives` from the existing TaskFieldCompleteness property would have produced a check that CANNOT FAIL: `_flatten` returned [] for the nested-dict shape every populated corpus block carries, so the loop body never ran and the property asserted nothing while reporting green.
discrepancies.affects: The current wave's exit criterion that the field class is actually closed
discrepancies.reason: Repaired inside the wave: total extractor, per-field ledger, builder-superset assertion, in-suite negative self-test. Exit criterion met rather than waived.

discrepancies.signal: A fresh dispatch inherits its predecessor's context-gauge reading. gauge.json held the second Commander's 18.4% (over the 15% hard band) and nothing refreshed it, because scripts/hooks/gauge_writer_hook.py is not wired into this worktree's .claude/settings.json. Every `advance` was blocked until the reading aged out of the reader's 30-minute window.
discrepancies.affects: Relaunch cost for every multi-dispatch issue, and the integrity of the governor's own record
discrepancies.evidence: gauge.json observed_at 2026-08-08T00:03:06.963Z, fill 0.184143, unchanged across the third dispatch's whole run; docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md; engine output 'CONTEXT GAUGE SILENT ... sampled 38m15s ago'
discrepancies.reason: The two available shortcuts are both dishonest — hand-writing a gauge record forges the instrument, and filing a refresh-request for an exhaustion this dispatch was not experiencing puts a false statement in the journal. The honest path costs a 30-minute wait, which quietly rewards the shortcuts. Needs a sanctioned way to invalidate an inherited reading.

discrepancies.signal: The completeness property's superset assertion closes the hole only for fields the ENGINE introduces. A field carried by a shipped template but built by neither `_build_amend_task` nor `append()` remains invisible to it.
discrepancies.affects: How completely the unrendered-field class is closed
discrepancies.evidence: Stated as the RESIDUAL LIMIT in the TaskFieldCompleteness docstring and now in docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Rendering section
discrepancies.reason: Stated rather than implied, and out of this issue's authorized scope. A forecast amendment is sufficient.

discrepancies.signal: The carried g1-reviewer finding — a separate false sentence at docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:138 that the pinned invariant chain would not catch — resolved benignly on inspection: the 'is not rendered' sentence IS the 'Known gap' sentence, so c1's conjunction does catch it.
discrepancies.affects: Whether postcondition c1 needed amendment through the engine
discrepancies.evidence: grep -n -i 'not rendered|never surfaced|known gap|directives' docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md — the only other `directives` mentions (lines ~237, ~288, ~290) are handoff and amend-op references that were already accurate
discrepancies.reason: A real risk correctly raised that resolved in the benign direction by inspection rather than by assumption. No issue is warranted; recorded so the resolution is not re-litigated.
